⚠ Please read before you begin — educational tool only, not a diagnosis

This self-assessment is provided for health education only. It is a simplified questionnaire based on TCM pattern-differentiation theory; it is not a medical diagnosis and does not replace an in-person consultation, which also relies on pulse-taking, tongue inspection and a full health history. Herbal formulas are classical references from the TCM literature — do not prepare, purchase or take any herbal formula on the basis of this page. Herbs can interact with prescription medication and some are unsafe in pregnancy or without professional preparation. Any formula should be prescribed and adjusted by a registered TCM practitioner who has assessed you in person. If you have a medical condition, are pregnant, or take prescription medication, speak with your physician or a registered practitioner first.

Tongue & Reports · 舌苔与报告

Add a tongue photo, imaging and lab results

In the clinic, tongue inspection is essential — and recent blood work or imaging often changes the picture. Add whatever is relevant; these files are what the paid review services above are based on. Files are previewed on your device only — nothing is uploaded or sent from this page; on the next page you'll get a ready-made email to the clinic to send them in together with your answers.

Tongue photo 舌苔照片

Natural light, no flash, no filters. Best in the morning before eating, drinking coffee or brushing your teeth — stick your tongue out fully and let it relax.

Imaging 影像资料

Reports or images from X-ray, ultrasound, CT or MRI that relate to your concern — the radiologist's written report is usually the most useful part.

Lab results 实验室结果

Recent blood work or other laboratory reports (PDF or photo of the report). The most recent results, plus any older ones you want compared, are the most helpful.

About your practitioner

Youwei Feng — Registered Traditional Chinese Medicine Practitioner & Registered Acupuncturist, Ontario, Canada

Before practising in Canada, Youwei Feng spent over 30 years as a Chief Physician （主任医师） at a Grade-A tertiary （三甲） hospital in China, with deep clinical and theoretical expertise in both Traditional Chinese Medicine and Western medicine — training that informs both this assessment and the clinic's lab and imaging interpretation service.

This assessment was prepared by Harmony TCM Wellness. A questionnaire can point in a direction, but real pattern differentiation happens in the clinic room — through conversation, pulse and tongue diagnosis, and your full health history. If your result concerns you, or you would like a formula prescribed properly for your constitution, book an in-person consultation. Acupuncture treatments at the clinic may be covered by extended health benefits, and direct billing is available.

Traditional Chinese Medicine is a regulated health profession in Ontario. For the regulator’s own introduction to TCM, see About Traditional Chinese Medicine — College of Traditional Chinese Medicine Practitioners and Acupuncturists of Ontario (CTCMPAO).

Prefer to be seen in person? Harmony TCM Wellness runs two in-person clinics, and at both you can book an in-person pattern assessment or acupuncture treatment — the same practitioner, the same standard of care, whichever clinic is more convenient for you. You can book online and pick your time directly, or use the appointment request form above and the clinic will confirm your time by email.

Disclaimer: This page is a health-education tool based on Traditional Chinese Medicine theory. It does not diagnose, treat or cure any disease, and its results are not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Herbal formula information is reproduced from classical TCM texts for reference; formulas must only be used under the guidance of a registered TCM practitioner. Never disregard professional medical advice or delay seeking it because of something you have read here. In an emergency, call 911.

Formula references used in the expert analysis are drawn from classical TCM texts — 《太平惠民和剂局方》, 《小儿药证直诀》, 《金匮要略》, 《医林改错》, 《医方集解》 — and standard TCM textbooks; individual prescriptions vary.
